Crisis Communications for {{fact:f:E-2021-001.client}}
Held by video conference. Minutes recorded by Julie Hill.

items: Julie Hill, Managing Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Amy Carter, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Nancy Suarez, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: The session was convened to review the engagement at about its midpoint and to agree how the communications work should change as the Company moves from response toward recovery. The discussion is summarized below in the order taken.

Nancy Suarez reported that inbound media and customer inquiries have slowed considerably since the summer, and that recent questions concern remediation more than the disruption itself. The group agreed that the reactive Q&A should be revised to lead with what has changed.
It was further agreed that superseded answers will be marked as retired in the inquiry log, not deleted, so that the record of what was said, and when, remains complete.

Megan Sutton confirmed that the operations team is prepared to describe the milestones completed to date in the next customer update. She asked that any step not yet signed off by operations be described as planned, and the group accepted that qualification without reservation.
Amy Carter will revise the draft accordingly. Nancy Suarez will prepare the distribution list and release-day checklist once a release date is set.

Julie Hill recommended that the talking points for the Company’s quarterly investor update acknowledge the disruption once, plainly, and then turn to the evidence of remediation. Megan Sutton noted that the finance team will wish to review any statement touching on cost or timing, and the group agreed that no such statement will be made without that review.

Given the lower volume of inquiries, the standing call will move from weekly to every other week once the customer update has been released. The inquiry log will be reviewed by email between calls, and any member of the group may request an earlier call should circumstances change.

Julie Hill observed that the designated spokespeople have had little occasion to speak on the matter since the summer, and proposed a refresher briefing before the holiday period. Megan Sutton agreed to propose suitable times, and Amy Carter will update the briefing note to reflect the revised Q&A.
